policy_title: Unlock North Sea oil, gas, and shale reserves
stated: Reform UK will fast-track licences for North Sea gas and oil, and grant shale gas licences on test sites for two years to enable major production once safety is proven, with local compensation schemes. This also includes fast-tracking licences for new oil and gas exploration in the North Sea to strengthen the UK's energy security and reduce reliance on imports.

source.quote: Cheap, Secure Energy for Britain Start fast-track licences of North Sea gas and oil. Grant shale gas licences on test sites for 2 years. Enable major production when safety is proven, with local compensation schemes. UK energy security remains vital, which is why Reform UK will fast-track new oil and gas exploration in the North Sea. This will also ensure a transition to new technologies that are proven to cut emissions, rather than damaging the economy to achieve unaffordable targets.

consolidated_from: Unlock North Sea oil, gas, and shale reserves
Fast-track licences for new oil and gas exploration in the North Sea

bearing_set.reason: Expanded domestic oil and gas supply is explicitly aimed at reducing import reliance, which directly bears on domestic energy prices and household energy bills — a core O2 indicator.
The policy explicitly targets energy security and reduced dependence on imported gas, which is a direct national-security/resilience dimension under O5.
Fast-tracking licences for new oil, gas, and shale extraction materially affects the UK's emissions trajectory and its credible pathway to climate commitments — a primary O6 indicator.
Cheaper and more secure domestic energy could materially reduce business input costs and support investment, bearing on productivity and real living standards beyond individual bills.
Expanded North Sea production raises receipts via the ring-fence Corporation Tax and Energy Profits Levy, materially affecting the funded/borrowed balance of public finances.

membership_note: Five fundamentals earn real verdicts: O6 is the dominant harm (emissions/environmental), O5 is the primary stated benefit (energy security), O2/O13 capture the household and aggregate economic channels, and O12 captures the fiscal revenue channel. No O4/O11/O9/O10 bearing clears the non-negligible bar.
